drafts.title: Keep the 1 Series’ premium, head-turning exterior while eliminating common functional exterior faults
drafts.description: Customers experience a car that looks sporty and classy and still delivers reliable exterior function: the styling remains a clear strength while common exterior problems (tyres, mirrors, lighting, build/trim) are reduced so exterior quality is not a source of owner complaints.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a market follow-up survey, at least 85% of owners rate the exterior styling positively (>=8/10) AND owner-reported exterior build/fit/finish or trim complaints are below 1% and owner-reported exterior lighting or mirror complaints are below 1% within the first 24 months; tyre-related noise/grip complaints are below 2% in the same period.
assumptions: Survey and complaint logging use a consistent definition of 'complaint' and cover a representative EU owner sample over 24 months.
Tyre fitment choices and supply can be aligned to achieve lower customer noise/grip complaints without unacceptable cost or emissions impacts.
uncertainties: Some exterior complaints stem from aftermarket tyre choices or local road conditions (potholes) which may limit achievable complaint reduction.
Customer tastes for styling may shift; survey timing may affect measured positivity.

drafts.title: Keep and strengthen seat comfort and interior quality while removing seat reliability and safety issues
drafts.description: Customers experience front seats that are clearly comfortable, supportive and easy to use (maintaining the current strengths) while reported problems — poor support, stitching/creasing, squeaks, electric seat faults and seat-belt issues — are eliminated so seats are both pleasant and reliable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a representative user study and owner follow-up: at least 90% of drivers rate front-seat comfort >=8/10; seat-related quality or safety faults (stitching, creaks, electric seat faults, seat-belt failures) are reported by no more than 2% of owners within 24 months; and 95% of participants report no awkward seating position or lower-back discomfort after a 2‑hour motorway drive.
assumptions: User study sample covers typical EU driver heights (160–190 cm) and includes both city and long-distance driving scenarios.
Warranty/quality handling processes are in place so that manufacturing/assembly causes of stitching or squeaks are addressed.
uncertainties: Perceived comfort has subjective variation; a small minority of users will always prefer different seat firmness/shapes.
Some reliability issues may be caused by rare installation faults or post-sale aftermarket changes.

drafts.title: Make the boot practical for everyday use and ensure the tailgate opens/closes reliably with convenient controls
drafts.description: Customers can load and secure everyday luggage easily and rely on the boot to open and close when expected, with a simple internal shut button provided.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Boot must accommodate two medium suitcases (55 x 40 x 23 cm) plus one cabin bag with the rear seats in place in all production variants; boot lid open/close operation (key/keyless/button) must show ≥99% success in a 1000-cycle durability test and owner-reported boot operation faults must be below 1% within the first 24 months. A clearly accessible internal boot-shut control is present on all variants.
assumptions: Suitcase dimensions above are representative of a common luggage standard used for testing.
Space allocation may vary between powertrain variants; measurement is performed on each marketed variant (including hybrid where applicable).
uncertainties: Hybrid/EV packaging constraints may reduce usable volume on some variants; where this occurs, vehicle function/packaging trade-offs must be communicated to customers.
Local repair or aftermarket attachments may affect boot usability.

drafts.title: Controls and displays must be safe and reliable to use while driving and climate control must offer independent, physical controls
drafts.description: Customers can operate driving‑critical displays and climate controls without distraction, experience dependable instrument functionality (no loss of key functions), and have standard independent driver/passenger temperature control with tactile controls for essential HVAC functions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a validated on-road usability test, drivers must complete common in-car tasks (e.g., change temperature, change audio source, check trip speed) with a mean glance duration ≤1.5 seconds and a task success rate ≥95%; display/system failures that remove key driving functions must occur in fewer than 1% of vehicles within 24 months; driver and passenger independent temperature control and physical buttons for essential HVAC functions are standard.
assumptions: Usability test tasks are defined and executed under representative driving conditions and follow established distraction test methods.
Physical control layout can be designed to avoid excessive cost or interface complexity.
uncertainties: Some advanced functions will still require touch input; trade-offs between minimalism and tactile controls will affect design decisions.
Software complexity and third-party apps may introduce sources of instability not fully controllable by vehicle UX design alone.

drafts.title: Deliver a premium-feeling, reliable key and locking experience that reliably remembers driver preferences
drafts.description: Customers feel the key is high-quality to hold and use, and the digital/keyless system reliably stores and recalls driver profiles and locking/unlocking behaviour without unpredictable locking or false alarms.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In owner follow-up and product trials: perceived key quality >=8/10 by at least 90% of participants; owner-reported key or locking-system faults (including forgetting driver preferences, unexpected re-locks, or alarm triggers) are below 1% within 24 months; digital key/profile recall failures occur in fewer than 1% of uses during initial ownership period.
assumptions: Surveys capture both physical key feel and digital-key behaviour; digital-key interoperability with common phone platforms is assumed.
Vehicles will ship with a robust default profile-handling implementation.
uncertainties: Third-party smartphone OS updates may affect digital-key reliability beyond BMW control.
Some rare locking faults may be caused by aftermarket actions or extreme user behaviour.

drafts.title: Increase perceived rear legroom and boot practicality in the EV successor so rear passengers feel genuinely comfortable
drafts.description: Customers experience a noticeably roomier rear seating area and a more practical boot in the successor EV variant, making the rear seat usable for adult passengers and the boot competitive for everyday luggage needs.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In customer trials of the successor EV variant, rear knee clearance (rear legroom) must increase by at least 50 mm versus the current F70 baseline and at least 90% of trial participants of height 175–185 cm report rear-seat comfort >=8/10; the boot must accommodate three medium suitcases (55 x 40 x 23 cm) with rear seats in place.
assumptions: The Neue Klasse / EV architecture delivers a longer wheelbase and packaging advantages enabling increased rear legroom and different battery packaging by the successor launch.
Measurement compares like-to-like variants (similarly equipped models) and uses representative occupant heights (175–185 cm).
uncertainties: Final battery packaging, crash-structure or regulatory constraints could reduce achievable interior gains.
Market acceptance depends on perceived trade-offs (e.g., ride, price).

drafts.title: Offer premium-feeling, non-leather interior material options that meet customer expectations for look and durability
drafts.description: Customers perceive sustainable, non-leather interior materials as premium and durable, so a leather-free or reduced-leather interior option no longer reduces perceived cabin quality.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In blinded material trials, at least 70% of participants rate the selected non-leather materials as 'premium' (>=8/10) for look and feel, and in accelerated wear testing these materials meet the same durability acceptance thresholds used for leather alternatives.
assumptions: Sufficient supply of high-quality recycled or bio-based materials is available at scale by successor launch.
Durability test standards for new materials are aligned with current internal thresholds for abrasion, staining and colour-fastness.
uncertainties: Some customer segments will continue to prefer traditional leather; regulatory or supplier changes could affect availability of materials.
Perception of 'premium' is subjective and may vary by market/culture.
